transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 15:00 PT | Duration 58 min | Recording on
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM) -- Ellen (Northwood Head of ML), Jonah (Infra Lead), Priya (Security), Marco (Product) 

Summary: quick audit-style migration demo to validate parity and identify friction points for a multi-vendor swap (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood). Focus areas: API surface parity, streaming + function calling, latency/cost tradeoffs, private/VPC constraints, security controls (KMS/SSO/SOC2). Agreed next steps and owners at end.

[00:00] MAYA: hey everyone, thanks for the time, appreciate it. quick round robin? real quick just name and role.
[00:12] ELLEN: Ellen Park, head of ML. we're looking to consolidate inference to reduce complexity, and also lower per-token cost on high throughput flows.
[00:18] JONAH: Jonah Li, infra. endpoints currently in GCP running a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic, some self-hosted Together bits. curious about network peering and VPC.
[00:26] PRIYA: Priya, security. SOC2 staged but want details around KMS, key separation, audit logs.
[00:32] MAYA: awesome. i'll give a 6-minute high level and then ravi will demo the console and a short parity example -- we'll call out rough cost + latency expectations.

[00:48] RAVI: ok real quick, we're gonna show the Redwood API call equivalence to OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. note: some things transcribed from our side might show as Redwood Opti-mize in the captions, but it's "Redwood Optimize".
[01:05] RAVI: first, basic generation. OpenAI folks use completion/ChatCompletion, Anthropic has Claude-style chat, Together is similar to OpenAI but with some different streaming chunks; Redwood exposes a unified /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoint and supports streaming, function/tool calling and structured JSON output.
[01:30] ELLEN: can you show an example streaming call? the current behavior we rely on is low-latency chunked tokens to the client.
[01:37] RAVI: yep. live shot: i'll fire a small prompt from the console and then show the equivalent curl.
[01:50] [01:50] RAVI: (starts demo) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v1","input":"Summarize the following document...","stream":true}' 
[02:07] (small pause, typing)
[02:15] RAVI: output streaming in. note: token latency depends on model, sequence length and batching. with the continuous batching we group small requests to improve throughput while preserving tail latency; you can set max_batch_delay in the routing policy.
[02:40] JONAH: that batching worries me a bit, at our p50 it's fine but p95 sometimes spikes. how can we guarantee latency for critical calls?
[02:49] RAVI: good q. you can pin to dedicated capacity (Reserved) with a lower batch window and hard SLOs, or route by policy so critical endpoints go to a low-latency pool. also we support a non-batching low-latency lane for enterprise. important: there's a tradeoff vs cost, because small batches raise per-token cost.
[03:15] ELLEN: so basically choose dedicated for p95-sensitive flows and hosted for lower priority?
[03:22] MAYA: yep that's the usual pattern. customers often run the product flows on Dedicated and blast naively cheap stuff on hosted.
[03:30] MARCO: what about signature compatibility? we have 50 microservices calling OpenAI/Anthropic; any adapter work?
[03:38] RAVI: we've got adapter guides and small shim code. for chat -> Redwood chat the fields mostly map. function calling is slightly different in schema but we provide examples for OpenAI and Anthropic style function payloads. we'll include those snippets in the parity sheet.

[03:58] [03:58] RAVI: switching gears to quality parity: we do model cataloging and a verified perf profile. for Together equivalents we suggest redwood-7b-q4 and for Anthropic-like higher-safety workloads redwood-13b-cls. exact mapping depends on your prompts.
[04:22] ELLEN: can you be specific about quantization? we saw artifacts when we tried q4 on our production prompts.
[04:29] RAVI: yeah great point. quantization can cause slight differences. our Optimize tool will recommend quantization profiles per-workload; for retrieval augmented generation we often avoid q4 for long-context heavy tasks. we'll flag prompt sets where we saw quality regressions and recommend a fallback model.
[04:52] PRIYA: security—how are customer keys handled? we need KMS, HSM options, and assurance that logs are tamper-evident.
[05:00] LEAH: hi i'm leah from CSM, we integrate with customer-managed KMS and support HSMs for Private deployments; audit logs are available with signed event digests and long retention add-ons. we'll share the SOC2 and architecture docs in the follow-up.
[05:18] PRIYA: do you keep any customer data for training?
[05:22] MAYA: no training on customer data for hosted unless you opt-in; Private deployments stay entirely in your VPC. we'll add the exact policy urls in the packet.

[05:34] [05:34] ELLEN: about private, we currently need an on-prem option for PHI flows — is that supported?
[05:40] RAVI: yes, we offer Private with an on-prem package. notable caveat: on-prem has a slightly different rollout cadence for kernel updates and quantization patches; we coordinate security patch windows.
[05:58] JONAH: networking: do you support VPC peering and private link? we have strict egress rules.
[06:05] RAVI: both VPC peering and private link supported; we can also do egress-only gateway endpoints so logs and metrics go to your monitoring stack.

[06:18] [06:18] ELLEN: thanks, can you talk about cost modelling? token pricing vs our current vendor. we're at roughly $0.0009/token on OpenAI for the backbone right now, including some volume discounts.
[06:30] MAYA: we'll run a simple delta in the parity spreadsheet. quick rule of thumb: Redwood's hosted is competitive and Dedicated reduces unit cost at higher commit levels; Optimize gives batching/caching suggestions that often reduce unit cost 20-40% on retrieval-heavy workloads.
[06:54] MARCO: for our microservices, we can't change all clients at once. what's the suggested rollout pattern?
[07:01] RAVI: blue/green routing is common: adapt the client via an adapter layer so you can flip traffic per service. Redwood Console supports route-based policies and can proxy to fallbacks to avoid errors during rollout.

[07:18] [07:18] RAVI: demo time: i'll show the Console routing UI—route groups, fallback models, and a simple canary flip. (screen share) here's a route we configured: /chat/product-summary route bound to redwood-13b-v1. you can set canary to 10% and automatic fallback to openai-legacy when error rate exceeds threshold. the fallback is pluggable.
[07:50] JONAH: wait fallback to OpenAI? doesn't that reintroduce vendor complexity?
[07:55] RAVI: right, fallback is optional and useful during rollouts. many customers prefer fallback to a cheaper hosted model rather than failing. it's a temporary safety valve.

[08:10] [08:10] ELLEN: any observability hooks? we need token-level cost attribution per route.
[08:17] LEAH: Console gives token-level breakdowns by route and model; we've got tracing hooks that propagate trace ids. you can export to datadog or prometheus.
[08:28] PRIYA: and access control? RBAC, SSO?
[08:31] MAYA: SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC at org/team/model levels. Private adds more fine-grained KMS policies.

[08:45] [08:45] RAVI: ok quick deep dive: KV cache and prefix caching. if you have repeated prefixes (like long system prompts), Redwood will cache the KV and reduce repeated compute; this is often a big cost saver for chat-heavy flows. note: cache hit rates vary by workload.
[09:06] ELLEN: interesting — our issue is a lot of short sessions with similar system messages; caching could help. any compatibility concerns with Anthropic-style higher-context safety prompts?
[09:16] RAVI: not usually. the cache is keyed by model+prefix+session metadata; we can expose cache stats via the Console.

[09:28] [09:28] MAYA: let's address the Together bit — we saw you're running some open-source together models. what do those endpoints look like?
[09:35] JONAH: they are dockerized endpoints behind a mesh, not perfectly stable. some degrade under load.
[09:40] RAVI: for Together equivalents we recommend a Redwood-managed variant with monitored autoscaling; for local dev you can keep Together and use Redwood adapters in prod to smooth differences.

[10:00] [10:00] (demo continues) RAVI: now i'll show a parity example: same prompt to Together, Anthropic, and Redwood equivalent and show token counts and latency.
[10:12] RAVI: (runs) Together: p50 85ms p95 320ms token count 1,120. Anthropic: p50 95ms p95 370ms token 1,110. Redwood (redwood-7b-q4f): p50 90ms p95 290ms token 1,115. raw traces attached after meeting.
[10:45] ELLEN: those numbers look promising, p95 improved vs Anthropic in that run. what's the confidence across other prompts?
[10:52] RAVI: this is a single-run sample, we'll run a wider bench (1k prompts across your top 20 flows). we'll include standard deviation and tail percentiles.

[11:05] [11:05] PRIYA: what about audit logs for inference inputs? do you redact PHI?
[11:12] LEAH: configurable redaction rules, and you can opt to never store inputs. Private deployments default to no persistence unless you enable retention.

[11:28] [11:28] MARCO: OK show me the SDKs. we use python and go heavily.
[11:33] RAVI: (shares sample) python client: from redwood import Client; c = Client(key=...); c.chat.create(...). go sdk similar. we also have adapter snippets for OpenAI/Anthropic naming.

[11:52] [11:52] ELLEN: for the adapter, do we need to maintain function-call schemas? we have a bunch of typed function specs.
[11:58] RAVI: you can keep your function specs; our adapter maps them. edge cases when schemas rely on provider-specific metadata, we'll help patch those.

[12:18] [12:18] (a bit of cross talk)
[12:25] ELLEN: caveat—cost aside, we need model output parity for legal/regulatory copy. any guarantees?
[12:31] MAYA: guarantees are hard; we provide regression detection via Optimize linked to your prompt sets/evals. we'll flag deviations and hold canary traffic until artifacts pass thresholds.

[12:50] [12:50] RAVI: quick note on quantization artifacts: sometimes names or tokens get split differently; we recommend running your golden prompts and checking diffs. Optimize can automate a battery of evals.

[13:10] [13:10] JONAH: is there a cost to keep OpenAI as a fallback? we need to budget for multi-vendor periods.
[13:16] MAYA: fallback usually incurs normal costs to that vendor; Redwood does not mark up the fallback provider's price, it's the vendor charge plus networking. we'll model that in the parity sheet.

[13:35] [13:35] PRIYA: security follow-up specifics — we need encryption at rest keys, key rotation policy, and proof of separation for audits.
[13:44] LEAH: noted. Maya will send the security packet; we'll schedule a dedicated security review call.

[14:00] [14:00] (Ravi shows Console audit view) RAVI: here's the audit timeline per-request, redactions are applied at write time. you can export signed audit bundles.

[14:22] ELLEN: operational question — how much client work to do a swap per microservice?
[14:27] RAVI: typically it's minimal: an adapter layer of ~20-60 lines per service if you keep the function contract; more if you rely on provider-specific features.

[14:40] [14:40] MARCO: SLA — do you offer enterprise SLOs for Dedicated?
[14:45] MAYA: yes SLA-backed Dedicated plans with latency and uptime targets. we'll include example SLA language in the follow-up.

[15:00] [15:00] (wrap up) MAYA: to recap: we'll share parity spreadsheet + adapter snippets, run the 1k-prompt bench, security packet and then schedule the pilot kickoff. owners and dates captured in action items. any other questions?
[15:15] ELLEN: one ask—can you include a sample rollback playbook?
[15:18] LEAH: yes we'll add that to the pilot kickoff doc.
[15:24] JONAH: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[15:26] MAYA: great — thanks all. we'll follow up via email with the packet.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), speaker labels sometimes short, filler words and brief crosstalk retained. Shared artifacts: parity-mapping-sheet.xlsx (link to be emailed), security-packet.pdf (link to be emailed), raw-bench-traces.tar.gz (to be shared after run).

End of recording.
